title: Jude and the Landfall
premise: Desert ranger Sebastian Brightwater pursues the thief Jude Vane across the Saltreach flats, only to watch the sea reclaim the desert and reveal the Cave of the Landfall, a drowned passage the legends say leads to the river's forbidden source beneath the Halvard Glacier. The thief he's chasing turns out to be a woman fleeing with her brother's stolen memory-stones — relics that record the dead — and Sebastian's own orders, sealed and unread, demand the stones' destruction and her capture. Bound together by the cave and the calving season's narrow window, they follow the river upstream through collapsing ice and the ghosts of Sebastian's own buried past, until he must choose between the duty that made him and the truth Jude carries. At the source, he opens his sealed orders, burns them, and chooses her — the two walking out through the last open route as the glacier closes behind them forever.
about_author: Sebastian Thornbury is the pen name of a former surveyor who spent six years mapping ephemeral waterways in coastal deserts before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels where landscapes behave like characters with long memories and shorter tempers.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Walked Backward
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Tracking Jude Vane across the Saltreach flats, Sebastian notes her strange habit of walking backward to erase her prints and wonders what theft is worth that discipline. The emotional beat is professional obsession curdling into curiosity — the first crack in a ranger's certainty.

chapters.title: Where the Sea Keeps Its Promises
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Cornered at the coast, Jude watches an impossible tide roll inland and flood the desert, revealing the Cave of the Landfall. She dives in with the memory-stones strapped to her chest. The beat is desperation sharpening into awe — she'd rather drown than surrender her brother's voice.

chapters.title: Admission Charged in Legends
chapters.summary: Sebastian follows her into the cave and both are sealed inside when the tide withdraws, the entrance collapsing behind them. Forced truce at lantern-light; Jude reveals the stones hum with her dead brother's recorded memories. The beat is wary alliance — two liars agreeing to stop lying about the small things.

chapters.title: The River That Remembers Upstream
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. They discover the cave's underground river flows toward the glacier — the only route out, but forbidden by ranger law. Sebastian conceals his sealed orders while navigating by childhood knowledge he's never explained. The beat is the first taste of shared purpose shadowed by his hidden betrayal.

chapters.title: What the Stones Said About Him
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A stone slips and plays a memory — of Sebastian, younger, standing at this same river with a woman who is now the Ranger-Commander who signed his orders. Jude says nothing. The beat is the quiet horror of realizing your enemy's loyalty was purchased with a secret.

chapters.title: Calving Season
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternate. They reach the glacier's mouth as the first calving begins — icebergs shearing off with cannon-cracks, the route open for days, not weeks. A near-death on the ice shelf forces Sebastian to save Jude with a ranger technique he was ordered never to teach outsiders. The beat is trust outpacing judgment.

chapters.title: Orders, Sealed and Burning
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sheltering from a storm, Sebastian finally opens his sealed orders: destroy the stones, capture Jude, and seal the source permanently — the Commander's own brother's memories are among them, and she wants them buried. He burns the orders instead. The beat is the quiet, terrifying freedom of treason.

chapters.title: The Forbidden Source
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. They reach the source: a cathedral of blue ice where the river is born, and where the stones can be played one final time at full voice. Jude lets her brother's last memory speak — and it names Sebastian's drowned sister, connecting their griefs. The beat is love arriving disguised as shared mourning.

chapters.title: What the Wilderness Forgives
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The Commander's pursuit party arrives through the calving route, led by Sebastian's old mentor. Sebastian stands between them and the source, confessing everything — his sister, his sealed orders, his choice. The mentor lets them pass, at cost. The beat is the climax: loyalty to truth over duty, spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs converging. As the glacier seals the route forever, Sebastian and Jude walk out together through the last opening, the stones' final echo fading behind them, a future unwritten ahead. The beat is resolution without absolution — the wilderness forgot nothing, but it forgave them anyway.
